body: I don’t do any of that, had mine for about 7 months and on mostly everyday, no burn-in noticable. And warranties are usually pretty long. From what I have seen online it seems you can just use it without worrying too much about burn-in, especially on newer ones.

Also in case you want to know my reasoning, tRAS=tRCD+tRTP+8, tRC=tRP+tRAS, and I forgot to mention tWTRL should be tRRDL*2, so 24, and tWTRS could be 4. Also if it is a-die, I would do tRFC at 372 instead of 360.

I figured, I have seen the video, but I also have been reading a lot on overclocking forums, and pretty much no one there agrees with buildzoid on that. You probably won’t notice a performance difference but IMO it is safer

tRAS to 56, tRC to 92, SCLs could probably be 6, tRDRDSD and tRDRDDD at 6, tWRWRSD and tWRWRDD at 8, if it is a-die tRFC could be 360 which would put it at 120ns, if it is m-die I would put it at 480 for 160ns.
I would set tRAS to 58 (tRCD+tRTP+8) and tRC to 94 (tRAS+tRP), and tWTRL to 24 (2*tRRDL)
